title: Aspect 1: Process vs Completion
description: Russian verbs come in pairs. The imperfective focuses on the process; the perfective focuses on completion. Today: recognizing the difference.
descriptionRussian: Русские глаголы существуют в видовых парах. Несовершенный вид (НСВ) описывает процесс; совершенный вид (СВ) описывает завершение.
intro: Russian verbs mostly come in pairs, and choosing between the two halves is the one thing about Russian that has no English equivalent at all. The difference is not when something happened but whether you are looking at it as an activity or as a finished job. Reading a book and getting a book read are two different verbs here. That distinction runs through the whole language.
rules: Russian verbs come in aspectual pairs. The imperfective (НСВ) focuses on the process: ongoing, repeated, or unfinished action. The perfective (СВ) focuses on completion: a single finished event with a result.
In the past tense, both aspects coexist. 'Я читал книгу' (was reading, was in the process) versus 'Я прочитал книгу' (read it through, finished it).
The perfective has no present tense. A perfective verb in 'present-tense' form actually describes a future completed action (covered in Lesson 7).
Look for context cues. Duration phrases (долго, час, всё утро) signal the imperfective. Completion or single-event cues (уже, наконец, за час) signal the perfective.
examples: Я читал книгу всё утро. (I was reading the book all morning.) НСВ читал: process, duration.
Я прочитал книгу. (I read the book through.) СВ прочитал: single completed event with a result.
Антон писал письмо два часа. (Anton was writing the letter for two hours.) НСВ писал: duration.
Антон написал письмо. (Anton finished the letter.) СВ написал: completion.
Маша готовила обед. (Masha was cooking dinner.) НСВ готовила: the process.
Маша приготовила обед. (Masha cooked dinner.) СВ приготовила: the result is ready.

items.promptEnglish: Masha was reading the book all morning.
items.hint: 'All morning' describes a duration. Which aspect focuses on the process?
items.explanation: 'Всё утро' is a duration cue. The imperfective читала describes the ongoing process: she was reading, the focus is on the activity itself, not on whether the book got finished.

items.promptEnglish: Anton finished the letter (wrote it through).
items.hint: 'Finished' signals completion. Which aspect describes a single completed event?
items.explanation: The English 'finished' or 'wrote it through' tells you the focus is on completion: the letter is done. The perfective написал marks a single finished event with a result.

items.promptEnglish: I was watching the film when she called.
items.hint: Something interrupted an ongoing action. Process or completion?
items.explanation: An ongoing action interrupted by another event takes the imperfective. Смотрел describes the activity that was already in progress when the call came.

items.prompt: Вчера Маша _____ обед, и мы поели.
items.promptEnglish: Yesterday Masha cooked dinner, and we ate.
items.hint: Did the dinner reach a finished state? Process or result?
items.explanation: The dinner is finished and was eaten: there is a result. The perfective приготовила marks completion.

items.promptEnglish: Lena was writing a letter all morning.
items.hint: Recall Q1.1's logic: duration cue → which aspect?
items.explanation: 'Всё утро' (all morning) is a duration cue, just like 'all morning' in Q1.1. The imperfective писала puts the focus on the activity itself. We do not know whether the letter was finished; the sentence reports what Lena was doing.

items.hint: Was this a single completed event, or a habit / process?
items.explanation: 'Bought' as an English past simple usually points to a single completed transaction. Купил is the perfective: one event, finished, the book is now his.

blanks: Маша _____ книгу за час и пошла спать. (Masha read the book through in an hour and went to sleep.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'За час' (in an hour) is a perfective cue: it measures the time the action took to be completed. Combined with 'пошла спать' (and went to sleep, a clear next event), the action is complete. Прочитала is the perfective.

errorCorrection.sentence: Раньше каждый вечер она послушала музыку дома.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: She used to listen to music at home every evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Каждый вечер signals a repeated habit, and habits take the imperfective: слушала. Послушала is perfective, framing the listening as one finished event, which clashes with a recurring action.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вчера я читал письмо за пять минут.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday I read the letter in five minutes.
errorCorrection.explanation: За plus a time span (за пять минут) measures how long it took to complete an action, so it demands the perfective: прочитал. Imperfective читал describes an ongoing process and cannot combine with за пять минут, which marks a bounded, finished result. Читал would be right with a bare duration instead ('Я читал письмо пять минут', meaning I spent five minutes reading), where the minutes measure process rather than completion.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вчера он написал доклад весь вечер.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday he was writing the report all evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Весь вечер measures the duration of an ongoing process, which calls for the imperfective: писал. Perfective написал presents the writing as one completed result, so it cannot stretch across a whole evening as a process. Написал would be correct with a completion frame instead ('Вчера он написал доклад', meaning he finished it yesterday), where the focus is the result.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I was writing a letter all day.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Весь день' (all day) is a duration cue. The imperfective писал describes the day-long process. The perfective написал would say the letter got finished, but the sentence does not report a completion.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton did the homework before lunch.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'До обеда' (before lunch) sets a deadline by which the action was finished. The perfective сделал marks completion: the homework is done. The imperfective делал would describe only the activity, without telling us it ended.

reviewVocab.definition: verbal aspect (the grammatical category that distinguishes process from completion in Russian verbs)
reviewVocab.example: Вид глагола — это одна из самых сложных тем в русском языке.

reviewVocab.definition: imperfective aspect (focuses on process, duration, repetition, or ongoing action; has all three tenses)
perfective aspect (focuses on a single completed event with a result; has past and future, but no present)
